answer: Open a request on the SailPoint support portal (or email support); reviews need an Expert Services contract (billable, typically 15-30 min per rule). Attach: (1) the rule XML (SailPoint template: XML declaration + sailpoint.dtd DOCTYPE, <Rule name=... type=...>, <Description>, code in CDATA, UTF-8) named exactly `Rule - {type} - {name}.xml`, e.g. `Rule - IdentityAttribute - Calculate Lifecycle.xml`; (2) validator output (e.g. `review_rule.py file.xml --report review.md`, plus SailPoint's community rule validator if used); (3) the tenant name (`acme-sb.identitynow.com` sandbox or `acme.identitynow.com` production); (4) approval for Expert Services to proceed. One rule per ticket unless rules must be deployed together. SLA: 24h for weekday submissions, next business day for weekends; ask 48h ahead for a specific deployment window. The review is an integrity check against guidelines, not a functional test, so test first (RDK/sandbox). Connector rules are different: created via `POST /connector-rules/v1` (JSON with escaped script and `signature`).

No. `context.` and `.getObjectByName()` are both on SailPoint's code-restriction list (blocked by the platform, reviewer checks R020/R021): there is no IIQ `context` in ISC. An IdentityAttribute rule receives only `log`, `idn` (IdnRuleUtil, read-only), `identity` and `oldValue`, and must return `attributeValue`. Use IdnRuleUtil: if you have the manager's ID, `idn.getIdentityById(managerId)` (returns `sailpoint.rule.Identity`); otherwise `idn.findIdentitiesBySearchableIdentityAttribute(attr, "Equals", value, sortAttr)` (Equals/StartsWith only, max 50 results). Null-check the result and the email before using them, wrap in try/catch that logs with `log.debug/warn` (never log the email itself as sensitive data), and return a value on every path. Also consider whether a transform can do it instead: transforms are preferred over IdentityAttribute rules because they need no SailPoint review.

Rejected (errors): `System.out.println` (not picked up by log aggregators; on the restriction list); declaring your own logger (`Logger.getLogger`, Log4j imports are restricted) - use the supplied `log`; logging sensitive data (passwords, personal data) - explicit rejection; logging full object serialization (`.toXml()` is prohibited; dumping whole identities/plans is flagged). Likely rejection/slower review (warnings): `log.error()` for informational messages - use `log.debug()` for debugging detail, `log.info()` for normal operation, `log.warn()` for non-critical issues, `log.error()` only for unexpected errors/critical failures; excessive or unnecessary logging calls (log sparingly but informatively). Also don't leave empty catch blocks: catch should log/handle. Note that for cloud rules (e.g. IdentityAttribute) logs are visible only to SailPoint personnel, so logging won't help you debug in production anyway.

Use the `-TEMP` procedure from SailPoint's versioning guidelines (one rule per use case, versioned copies like `v2`/`new`/`copy` are not supported). 1) Submit the new logic as a separate rule named `<original name>-TEMP` (file `Rule - BeforeProvisioning - <name>-TEMP.xml`) and get it approved/deployed. 2) In your change window, switch the source's BeforeProvisioning rule reference to the TEMP rule and validate. 3) Submit the update of the original rule under the same name with the same logic. 4) Once deployed, switch the source back to the original. 5) Ask SailPoint to delete the TEMP rule. If you just need a timed deployment, tell SailPoint at least 48 hours ahead; for weekend go-lives deploy to sandbox first and promote to production yourself with sp-config export/import (`POST /sp-config/v1/export` / `/import`), which carries the approved signature without a new review. Remember BeforeProvisioning rules modify `plan` in place and return nothing.

Two errors. 1) `"Contains"` is not a supported operation: IdnRuleUtil searches accept only `"Equals"` or `"StartsWith"` (check R072; it throws otherwise). Signature is `int countIdentitiesBySearchableIdentityAttribute(String attributeName, String operation, String value)`, and the attribute must be a searchable identity attribute. For email uniqueness use `"Equals"`; for account values prefer `idn.attrSearchCountAccounts(List sourceIds, attr, "Equals", List values)` on a searchable account attribute, or `idn.isUniqueLDAPValue(identityNameOrId, applicationNameOrId, attr, value)` for AD/LDAP. 2) Looping over `identity.getLinks()` iterates over accounts (cache bloat; check R060) - replace with one targeted call such as `idn.getFirstAccountNativeIdentity(app, identityName)`, `idn.getAccountByNativeIdentity(app, id)` or `idn.getAccountAttribute(app, nativeId, attr)` (app = source name + ` [source]`). Also avoid idn lookups inside loops (R061); a bounded uniqueness retry loop (value, value1...) is the documented pattern but keep it short. Null-check returns and always return a value.

No. ISC does not import IIQ XML: every object is rebuilt in ISC (UI, REST API, or sp-config JSON for supported object types). Treat it as a re-architecture done in phases with IIQ and ISC side by side. Export the IIQ XML anyway as input for analysis (`python3 scripts/analyze_iiq.py iiq-export/ --plan migration-plan.md`), which classifies each object as direct/adapt/none and names the ISC equivalent. Rough mapping: Application -> Source + connector/schema/correlation config/Create Account; Rule -> transform, cloud rule (reviewed by SailPoint), connector rule (`POST /connector-rules/v1`) or configuration; Workflow -> ISC Workflows (no BeanShell; triggers/actions) plus access request config. Rules you keep must be rewritten without `context`, rule libraries, JDBC/HTTP, and pass review. SailPoint offers an Upgrade Assessment and, since June 2026, SailPoint Agentic Acceleration with an AI tool (Virtual Architect) that converts IIQ config, workflows and policies into an ISC starting point via its forward deployed engineers - still a starting point, not an import.

ISC has no AfterProvisioning rule type, so it becomes an ISC Workflow (level: adapt). Trigger: Provisioning Completed (`idn:post-provisioning`, fire-and-forget), whose payload contains `accountRequests[]` with `source`, `accountId`, `accountOperation`, `provisioningResult`, plus `recipient`, `errors`. Add a filter/Compare step so it runs only when the source is your AD source, `accountOperation` is Disable and the result succeeded. Then create the ticket with the HTTP Request action (`sp:http`) against the ServiceNow Table API (OAuth/basic credentials in the action), or the ServiceNow action (`sp:snow`) if available in your tenant. Optional: Get Identity (`sp:get-identity`) for more context, Send Email (`sp:send-email`) on failure. Do not port the BeanShell: workflows don't run scripts, and any IIQ `context`/HTTP code is not allowed in cloud rules either. Alternatively subscribe an external service to the same event trigger. Test with the workflow test payload before enabling.

All three are 'adapt'. Correlation rule -> the source's correlation configuration (attribute pairs, Equals, first match wins); only if that cannot express it, a Correlation cloud rule returning a Map with `identityAttributeName`/`identityAttributeValue` (needs SailPoint review). Creation (IdentityCreation) rule -> no ISC equivalent rule: use the HR source's identity profile attribute mappings with transforms (attributes are recomputed on every refresh, so logic must be idempotent; lifecycle state via a transform or IdentityAttribute rule). ResourceObjectCustomization -> no customization rule in ISC: apply transforms where the value is consumed (identity profile mappings); for Delimited File/JDBC sources use a BuildMap/JDBCBuildMap connector rule (runs on the VA, no `context`); for SaaS connectors a connector customizer. Prefer configuration and transforms first: transforms need no SailPoint review, while every cloud rule costs Expert Services review time. Build order: source, correlation, first aggregation, compare identities with IIQ, then identity profile/transforms, then lifecycle states.

All three have no ISC equivalent (level: none) and need redesign. QuickLinks -> Request Center for access requests; for custom self-service actions, ISC Forms plus a Workflow (external trigger or Form submitted). Custom objects (sailpoint.object.Custom) -> lookup tables in transforms (`lookup` transform) for mapping data, identity/source attributes, or an external store you call from workflows (HTTP Request). Plugins -> an external application on the ISC APIs (SailPoint UI Development Kit), or workflows/event triggers for background logic. Also related: custom task executors and Run Rule tasks become scheduled workflows or external jobs on the ISC API. Rule libraries don't exist either (inline code). Inventory these early because they are typically the largest redesign items; retire unused ones during the IIQ cleanup step before migrating.

Both IIQ rule types are deprecated in ISC (the reviewer rejects them, check R005), so replace them with configuration. Business roles (Bundle type business) with an IdentitySelector rule -> ISC roles with membership criteria (identity attributes, account attributes, entitlements, combined with AND/OR) - level adapt; required/permitted roles and role inheritance must be flattened, and IT roles become access profiles (single source) or role access. If the selector logic can't be expressed, derive a helper identity attribute (transform) and base criteria on it. CertificationExclusion rules -> campaign filters on the ISC campaign (manager, source owner, search, role composition, machine account campaigns), excluding identities/access by attributes, sources, entitlements; certifier rules -> campaign reviewer type. Build roles in phase 5 (after sources and identity profiles) and campaigns last, after SOD policies.
